sections.h2: What kind of place is Johnson County for a home seller?
sections.html:
Johnson County is a small, rural county in east central Georgia with Wrightsville as its seat. The legislature carved it out of Washington, Laurens and Emanuel counties on December 11, 1858, and the county's own history page says it is within driving distance of Macon, Savannah, Augusta and Milledgeville. The present courthouse went up in 1895 and sits on the National Register of Historic Places, so downtown Wrightsville has an older core around it.

Two other communities matter when you describe a property. Kite was laid out in the 1890s and still has a small museum in a former Masonic lodge. Adrian is split by the Emanuel County line, which runs through town in the shape of a Z, so two neighbors on the same street can pay tax to different counties. If your parcel is near Adrian, check which county's tax commissioner bills it before you call anyone.

The Census Bureau lists 303.02 square miles of land and about 30 residents per square mile in 2020. That is a lot of open ground per household, which is why many Johnson County sales involve acreage, timber or a house on a farm road rather than a subdivision lot.

sections.h2: What do the Census numbers say about Johnson County housing?
sections.html:
Home values in Johnson County sit far below the Census figures for Jones and Lamar counties.

The county lost residents between 2010 and 2020 and has recovered only a little since. Residents aged 65 and over make up 20.9% of the population, and 3,217 households were counted in 2020-2024. A seller here is often an heir, a retiree or an owner of a house that has sat empty, and the buyer pool is thin compared with Macon. Zero building permits in 2025 also means few new comparable sales to point to.

sections.h2: Which Johnson County offices handle what?
sections.html:
Johnson County splits tax work between two offices in the same building at 2484 West Elm Street, Wrightsville, GA 31096.

  • Tax Commissioner: bills, collects, issues payoff figures and takes vehicle registration. Phone (478) 864-2565 ext. 1, open 8:00 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. Monday through Friday, with online payment through the county's tax commissioner site.
  • Tax Assessors: values, returns, exemptions and appeals. Phone (478) 864-3325 ext. 2, with parcel records on qPublic.
  • Clerk of Superior Court: recorded deeds, at 2557 East Elm Street, (478) 864-3484.
  • Probate Court: estates, at (478) 864-3316, which matters if an owner has died and the title is still in their name.

The county's tax commissioner page also carries a relief notice for damaged timber cut after Hurricane Helene. To use it, fill out the form from the Georgia Forestry Commission, attach the documentation the form lists, and submit it to the tax commissioner. Anyone selling timberland should ask whether a claim is open before closing.

sections.h2: How does Johnson County value a house, and how do I appeal?
sections.html:
The Board of Tax Assessors values every parcel as of January 1, and the tax is levied on 40% of that fair market value. Returns for real estate go to the assessors' office between January 1 and April 1 in years when the property changed or was acquired. An owner who skips a required return faces a 10% penalty on the value not returned, plus interest.

If you disagree with the value on your notice, the written appeal goes first to the Board of Assessors, and the Georgia Department of Revenue says it must be postmarked within 45 days of the date the notice was mailed. In that first letter you pick a route. The department's list is the county Board of Equalization, a hearing officer or an arbitrator, and the county's page adds Superior Court as another path. Ask the assessors for the state's uniform appeal form.

Refunds work on a longer clock. A written request for taxes that were erroneously or illegally collected must start within three years of payment, and a refund tied to a successful appeal is processed on its own once the final value is set.

sections.h2: What homestead and timber breaks apply in Johnson County?
sections.html:
The Department of Revenue's county fact sheet states that Johnson County offers no local homestead exemptions, so owners rely on the statewide ones. A first-time applicant files with the county, and the application must arrive by April 1 of the first year the exemption is claimed. A late application starts the following year, and once granted the exemption renews automatically until the owner moves or changes ownership.

  • Homestead requires that you own and occupy the home as your legal residence.
  • The assessors make the final decision on eligibility.
  • Personal property returns are due every April 1 whether or not anything changed.
  • A mobile home needs a location permit within 30 days of placement, then a renewal between January 1 and April 1 each year.

Voters in any Georgia county may adopt a freeport exemption for commercial and industrial inventory, which the Revenue Department says is requested through the board of assessors in the same window as returns.

sections.h2: When is the Johnson County tax bill due?
sections.html:
Georgia's default due date is December 20, but a county may move it to December 1 or November 15, or bill in installments. Ask the tax commissioner at (478) 864-2565 ext. 1 which date applies to your parcel, because the county's general information page does not print one.

By state rule, the bill gives you 60 days from the postmark before interest accrues, and delinquent balances can pick up penalties after that. Bills are sent to the owner of record, so a mortgage servicer will not necessarily see yours. If you moved, send the tax commissioner and assessors a written change of address, because the county sends tax notices to the last known address on file.

One rule catches sellers off guard. The Revenue Department states that whoever owned the property on January 1 is responsible for that year's tax, even if the house sells in January. Georgia has no refund for part-year owners, so buyer and seller usually settle the year between themselves at closing.

sections.h2: How do I sell a Johnson County house that owes back taxes?
sections.html:
Start with a written payoff from the tax commissioner, then ask the Clerk of Superior Court whether a lien has been recorded against the parcel. Unpaid county tax can become a lien on the general execution docket in the clerk's office, and the commissioner can levy and sell the property for nonpayment. The commissioner's tax sales page is the place to see how those sales are run.

A title company or closing attorney can pay the commissioner from the seller's proceeds and clear the lien at closing. If the owner has died, the estate has to be opened through Probate Court before anyone can sign a deed. A buyer who purchases as-is and handles the paperwork can shorten that path, but the tax payoff, the recorded deed and any estate filing are the same steps in every Johnson County sale.

faqs.q: Who sends the property tax bill in Johnson County, Georgia?
faqs.a: The Johnson County Tax Commissioner bills and collects county, school and state property tax from its office at 2484 West Elm Street in Wrightsville. The phone is (478) 864-2565 ext. 1. The assessors at (478) 864-3325 ext. 2 set the value, so call them for questions about the number rather than the bill.

faqs.q: Does Johnson County have its own homestead exemption?
faqs.a: No. The Georgia Department of Revenue's fact sheet for the county says no local homestead exemptions are offered, so owners apply for the statewide exemptions. The application must be received by April 1 of the first year you want the break.

faqs.q: How long can I appeal my Johnson County assessment?
faqs.a: You have 45 days from the date the assessment notice was mailed. The appeal is written, goes to the Board of Tax Assessors first, and must state which route you choose. Ask the assessors for the uniform appeal form.

faqs.q: What is the median home value in Johnson County?
faqs.a: The Census Bureau lists $94,900 as the median value of owner-occupied homes for 2020-2024, with 75.9% of housing units owner-occupied. Median gross rent was $647 and median household income was $51,028.

faqs.q: Do I owe the full year of tax if I sell in January?
faqs.a: Yes, the owner on January 1 is responsible for that year's bill. The Revenue Department says Georgia does not refund part-year owners, so the closing statement usually divides the cost between buyer and seller.
